analysis.answer_text: Okay, let’s steady that connection. I’ll walk through a clear sequence you can follow.First, move closer to your router and watch if the drops stop, since weak signal can look like random disconnects. Next, restart your router and modem
analysis.reply_text: | If you don’t know the router password, you’ve got a few options. First, check the router itself. There’s often a sticker on the bottom or back with the default username and password, sometimes labeled “admin” or “wireless key.” Next, try the default login listed in the manual or on the manufacturer’s website. If it’s been changed and you can’t recover it, you can reset the router with the small reset button, usually held for about ten seconds, which restores factory defaults, though you’ll have to set up Wi‑Fi again. You can also check if your internet provider gave you a management app or a customer portal where you can see or change the password. And if none of that works, contacting your provider is the safest next step.
